tapeLine: Latest US close is Wednesday 25 November: S&P 500 −0.25% to 7,182.78; Nasdaq Composite −0.62% to 23,585.80; Dow +0.33% to 50,182.95 (CNBC; Investing.com, 25 Nov). Markets were shut Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen today for a session ending 1:00 p.m. ET (TipRanks, 27 Nov).
matters:
US index futures were sharply higher before today’s half-day session. TipRanks had Nasdaq-100, S&P 500 and Dow futures up 2.38%, 1.74% and 1.30% as of 5:41 a.m. ET; other early-morning snapshots differ because they were taken at different times (TipRanks; SSBCrack; BeInCrypto, 27 Nov). Reports attribute the move to a rebound in chipmakers and other tech shares after Wednesday’s intraday flush, with easing worries about the profitability of AI spending; BeInCrypto put S&P 500 futures above 7,300 even as Nvidia sits on S&P Global’s CreditWatch negative (BeInCrypto; SSBCrack, 27 Nov).

Thursday’s overseas sessions set that up. Per AP, the Nikkei 225 rose about 0.9% to 57,499.16, Taiwan’s Taiex 2.5% and the Hang Seng 1.2%, and the Kospi recovered slightly after a 6.2% drop the day before; AP and Yahoo Finance said the new US Section 301 tariff proposals were seen as less damaging than feared (AP via US News and BNN Bloomberg; Yahoo Finance, 26 Nov). In Europe, Frankfurt and Paris were up nearly 2% and London about 1.6% at midday per Yahoo Finance. No major US data or earnings are scheduled today, and volume is expected to be thin (TipRanks, 27 Nov).

overnight: US futures — Nasdaq-100 +2.38%, S&P 500 +1.74%, Dow +1.30% as of 5:41 a.m. ET; a premarket snapshot, not a close (TipRanks, 27 Nov).
Asia, Thursday — Nikkei 225 about +0.9% to 57,499.16; Taiex +2.5%; Hang Seng +1.2%; Kospi slightly higher after a 6.2% fall on Wednesday (AP via US News; BNN Bloomberg, 26 Nov).
Europe, Thursday — Frankfurt and Paris up nearly 2% and London about 1.6% at midday (Yahoo Finance, 26 Nov); full-day closes not confirmed and left out.
deals: Lukoil International / US-led consortium — group led by Eldridge, with the US International Development Finance Corporation, UAE-based Catena Investment Holding and Xtellus Partners, agreed to buy Lukoil’s international assets; per Reuters the deal involves $10 billion in securities, with the assets valued around $16 billion. Subject to US Treasury approval (BNN Bloomberg; The National, 25–26 Nov).
PHINIA / FMP Group — PHINIA agreed to acquire FMP Group, the Australian business behind Bendix brakes and Trico wipers, in a deal reported at US$160 million (Australian Car Mechanic, 26 Nov).
APR Corp. / Brand 501 — APR agreed to acquire Dr. Melaxin operator Brand 501 for about 390 billion won, disclosed in a regulatory filing Thursday (World Today Journal, 27 Nov).

regime.tag: A tech-led futures rebound into a thin, holiday-shortened session, after Wednesday's intraday flush and a closed Thursday.
regime.sizing: Today closes at 1:00 p.m. ET for stocks and 2:00 p.m. ET for bonds; liquidity is thin by schedule.

secondOrder: Futures are pointing to a gain larger than Wednesday’s whole S&P decline, on a day with no data and a short session. Thursday’s overseas rally was read as relief that the tariff proposals were milder than feared, while the proposals themselves have not changed. Observations, not forecasts.
